title: Enquiries regarding EU funding for the Digital Freedom Fund and grants to the  Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte
text:
QUESTION

PE782.726v01-00
Question for written answer E-000002/2026
to the Commission
Rule 144
Alexander Jungbluth (ESN)
Subject:
Enquiries regarding EU funding for the Digital Freedom Fund and grants to the
Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte
The Digital Freedom Fund (DFF) receives funding for the digiRISE project (2022-2025) from
the EU’s Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values programme, which it says is used to support
processes that safeguard digital rights. The Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte (Society for Civil
Rights, GFF) has been funded by the DFF since 2018, receiving an estimated total of EUR
400 0001 for projects in areas such as digital rights, migration and algorithm transparency.
The GFF also uses the funding to bring legal action against political opponents2 or
governments3. In its reply to written question E-002215/2025, the Commission confirmed that
funding had been granted to the DFF for digiRISE, but explicitly stated that: ‘The project
does not foresee the possibility of redistributing EU funding to third parties.’4 That statement
contradicts the facts set out above.
1.
What does the Commission mean by ‘redistributing EU funding to third parties’ in this
specific context?
2.
How does the Commission ensure that EU funding for digiRISE does not free up or
complement private funding of the DFF (‘fungibility’) to finance other, potentially
politically sensitive, GFF activities such as legal action against governments of EU
Member States?
3.
Does the Commission take the view that EU funding for the DFF – which supports the
GFF with strategic litigation in the abovementioned areas – is compatible with the
principle of political neutrality of EU funding, even if the support concerned is indirect?
Submitted: 2.1.2026
1
https://freiheitsrechte.org/en/ueber-die-gff/finanzen-transparenz.
2
https://freiheitsrechte.org/spende-afd-gutachten.
3
https://freiheitsrechte.org/ueber-die-gff/presse/pressemitteilungen-der-gesellschaft-fur-freiheitsrechte/pm-
spyware-anzeige.
4
https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2025-002215-ASW_EN.html

--- ANSWER ---

EN
E-000002/2026
Answer given by Mr McGrath
on behalf of the European Commission
(20.2.2026)
The Financial Support to Third Parties provided for in the Financial Regulation1 allows, if
expressly foreseen in the grant agreement, the beneficiaries to provide financial support to
entities that are not part to the grant agreement. This is possible if done in line with the
provisions of the Financial Regulation. The DigiRise project does not foresee this possibility
to redistribute funding.
The DigiRise project is funded through an action grant, whereby funding is provided to
implement the project described in the agreement. The costs of implementing the action are
set out in a budget that is part of the grant agreement. The grant is paid to the beneficiaries
only if the action is implemented in line with the agreement, if the foreseen activities are
implemented and the deliverables approved by the Commission. Funding cannot be used for
other purposes that the ones listed in the grant agreement.
The general objective of the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values (CERV)2 funding
programme adopted by the EU Member States in the Council and by the European Parliament
is to protect and promote rights and values as enshrined in the Treaties and the Charter of
Fundamental Rights. Funding is provided in full transparency and in line with the Financial
Regulation after a highly competitive process following open calls published on the Funding
and Tender portal. Proposals are evaluated against award criteria such as quality and
relevance in order to make sure that they implement the objectives of the funding programme.
1 Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 September 2024 on
the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union (recast) ELI:
http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2509/oj.
2 Regulation (EU) 2021/692 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 April 2021 establishing the
Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values Programme and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1381/2013 of the European
Parliament and of the Council and Council Regulation (EU) No 390/2014 ELI:
http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/692/oj.
